title: Why Does Brazil Speak Portuguese? The 1494 Line
desc: On 7 June 1494, at Tordesillas in Spain, Castile and Portugal agreed a line from pole to pole, 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands: new lands to the west for Castile, to the east for Portugal. It moved the line set by Pope Alexander VI's 1493 bull, 100 leagues out. Later maps placed the line anywhere from about 42° to 50° W. title: Why Chile Is So Long and Thin
desc: Chile runs 4,270 km from north to south but is only 177 km wide on average. The two halves of that shape have two different explanations: the Andes made Chile thin, and nearly four centuries of conquest, war and treaties made it long. title: How Istanbul Ended Up on Two Continents
desc: Istanbul spans Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus. Greek settlers from Megara first founded Chalcedon on the Asian shore; according to Strabo, an oracle later told the founders of Byzantium to build "opposite the blind", which they took to mean Chalcedon, and they settled the far better European site.
